Title: Tamil‐Brāhmī
Abstract (start): Tamil‐Brāhmī is the earliest script found in the extreme south of India in which Tamil inscriptions are written; it was an adaptation from the Brāhmī script used in the Prakrit inscriptions of Aśoka (r. ca. 272–236 bce ). The simple phonemic system of Tamil resulted in the adaptation of the script. Both the scripts differed in depicting graphically the basic consonants with or without the vowel “a.” Tamil‐Brāhmī was used in all early Tamil inscriptions found in rock‐shelters and also on pottery from excavated sites. Its advent is dated to the middle of the third century bce at the earliest.

The burials were recovered from three megalithic graves containing iron weapons and horse trappings, pottery and terracotta figurines, stone blades, pieces of copper, and faunal remains of domesticated species. A Re-Examination of the Palaeolithic Archaeological Record of Northern Tamil Nadu, South India
Abstract (start): An expanded dissertation which uses a variety of approaches to examine the use of resources and evidence for human behaviour in a classic area for the Indian Palaeolithic'. Sections that examine the Quaternary environment, the archaeological record, the ethnographic record and hominid adaptive strategies are illustrated throughout with drawings of lithics and photographs of sites which cover the entire Palaeolithic period.

Title: Structure and society in early South India : essays in honour of Noboru Karashima
Abstract (start): This collection of essays in honor of Noboru Karashima, whose vast research has uncovered much of the history of the Pallava-Cola and Vijayanagara eras in south Indian history, a period that spans the eighth to the sixteenth centuries. The essays address the emergence of rural and urban societies and state systems in the region and demonstrate the richness of contemporary research, particularly that based on the study of pre-colonial south Indian temple inscriptions.
